did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens with a call to Zion: “Arise, shine,” presenting her light as a sign that the glory of the LORD shines upon her.
Did you know? In contrast to the darkness and gloom covering the earth and the nations, the LORD shines upon Zion, and His glory is seen over her.
Did you know? The vision of redemption describes both the return of Zion’s children from afar and the nations of the world streaming to her with their wealth.
Did you know? Among the gifts brought to Zion are gold and frankincense, and those who bring them proclaim the praises of the LORD.
Did you know? The chapter mentions the flocks of Kedar and the rams of Nebaioth, described as serving Zion and going up acceptably on the LORD’s altar.
Did you know? Those returning to Zion are compared to flying clouds and doves returning to their windows—images of swift movement and coming home.
Did you know? Zion’s gates are described as being open continually, day and night, to receive the wealth of the nations and their kings.
Did you know? The chapter describes simple building materials being replaced with more valuable ones: bronze with gold, iron with silver, wood with bronze, and stones with iron.
Did you know? In the latter part of the chapter, the LORD Himself is described as Zion’s everlasting light, surpassing the light of the sun and moon.
Did you know? The chapter ends with a promise of tremendous growth: “The least shall become a thousand,” together with the declaration that the LORD will hasten it in its time.
